summary: Finite two-base coherence checkpoint: ten new declarations (one construction, nine lemmas), eight API additions and six acceptance examples, including an explicit native scalar-action bridge and actual quotient/coefficient naturality. All incoming mathematical contracts and all source issues/routes/keys are retained. Partial pointed-moduli roadmap. Adds twelve consumed declaration-sized inputs for ordinary R-bidual reflexivity of the actual polynomial section ideal, with explicit inverse F↦F(incl), native evaluation equivalence and dual reflexivity through the existing Mathlib instance. All inherited contracts remain, all eight stages stay partial, and arbitrary coefficient-module Hom exchange, higher Ext, completion and family geometry remain required. The actual polynomial coefficient-module Hom comparisons D⊗_A M≃Hom_R(J,R⊗_A M) and J⊗_A M≃Hom_R(D,R⊗_A M) are R-linear, canonical on pure tensors, natural for arbitrary A-linear coefficient maps and compatible with native bidual evaluation when M=A. Signed coordinate lemmas and universal transpose exactness give bijectivity for every M without a flatness assumption; no higher Ext, relative stable-reflexivity or geometric closure is inferred. The actual R-module Hom cochains for the polynomial section ideal and dual are specified with correct alternating phases, signed augmentation cycles and zero native positive cohomology for every coefficient module. The augmented projective-resolution/Ext identification remains required. This checkpoint supplies the actual native projective resolutions of the polynomial section ideal and its dual; the higher Ext and geometric comparisons remain open. The actual categorical Hom-complex comparison is now checked, coefficient-natural in every degree and linked to both native Mathlib positive Ext interfaces. Ext_R^{n+1}(J,R⊗_A M)=Ext_R^{n+1}(D,R⊗_A M)=0 for every M without flatness. The next frontier is the exact Appendix/Ile relative stable-reflexivity and two-base completion theorem, then the pointed completed-local hull, family/sheaf descent and arbitrary-base approximation. All MC.0–MC.7 geometric obligations remain. The exact canonical second exchange is now identified as Φ_D,M∘(η⊗id_M)=Θ_J,M. Together with inherited Θ_D,M and both coefficient-universal Ext vanishings, the polynomial model meets all four conditions of Knudsen Appendix Theorem2(1); over noetherian A this gives the source’s relative stable-reflexivity conclusion for J (and symmetrically D). Actual positive Ext into R is separately transported through the native right tensor unit in both Mathlib Ext interfaces. The suggested file does not invent a generic stable-reflexivity predicate. The remaining work is its reusable owner-level formulation, Proposition6’s two-base completion comparison (including Ŝ-module coefficients), pointed completed-local hull, family/sheaf descent and arbitrary-base approximation. All eight stages remain partial. This continuation supplies the actual completed coefficient algebra and its exact two-base tensor quotient, keeping the full relative completion theorem open. Finite quotient two-base coefficient comparison for every completed-base module, with finite-generation kernel control and actual Hom target transport. The actual finite tensor diagrams over A and Â now have an A-linear natural isomorphism and native inverse-limit comparison with forward/inverse projections, uniqueness and cone transport. This compares limits of finite tensors only; ordinary tensor commutation with completion and the full relative completion theorem remain distinct required inputs. The completed-action checkpoint adds twenty declarations (five constructions and fifteen promoted API lemmas), fifteen APIs and fifteen tests. It constructs the actual Â-linear finite tensor diagram, its restriction comparison, the A-linear equivalence with the restricted native completed limit, the transported Â-action on the original A-limit with its actual scalar tower, and an Â-linear equivalence with completed-linear projection formulas. All 406 incoming node objects remain identical; ordinary tensor/limit interchange and full two-base relative completion remain open.

nodes.title: Moduli stacks of pointed curves
nodes.statement: Define a single moduli pseudofunctor CurvesModuli(ε,g,n), ε=smooth or stable, on schemes. Its fibre over S is the groupoid of parent curve families f:C→S, proper flat finitely presented of pure relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibres of arithmetic genus g and an ordered list of n disjoint sections through the relative smooth locus. In the stable flavour fibres are nodal and ω_{C/S}(Σsᵢ) is relatively ample; the smooth flavour is the full subcategory with f smooth. Arrows are marking-preserving S-isomorphisms; pullback is scheme-theoretic base change with its canonical associator. Write M_{g,n} and M̄_{g,n}. This is a groupoid-valued functor; no coarse or fine representability is built into its definition.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Use the parent’s stable-pointed and smooth-curve family data, without redefining stability.
Form the fibre groupoid using marking-preserving relative isomorphisms.
Use pullback universal properties to obtain coherent reindexing; the effective-descent assertion is a separate node.
acceptance: The genus-zero stable range begins at n=3; a two-pointed rational curve is excluded.
A self-node contributes two normalization flags to stability.

proofSteps: Use the unique morphisms supplied by pullback universal properties; their composites have equal projections, hence agree.
Import the parent’s base-change preservation of geometric genus, nodality, smooth sections and log-dualizing ampleness.
acceptance: Composition is coherent, not asserted definitionally equal.

nodes.title: The universal curve with an arbitrary extra section
nodes.statement: Define Z̄_{g,n} over M̄_{g,n} by an object (C/S;s₁,…,sₙ;Δ), where Δ:S→C is an arbitrary additional section. It may hit a node or an old marking. For S→M̄_{g,n} classified by C/S, the fibre product S×_{M̄} Z̄ is canonically C. This representable proper flat nodal morphism is the universal curve; it is smooth over the smooth base only after restricting the total space to smooth fibres.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: The groupoid of pairs (T→S, a section of C_T/T) is the representable fibre category of C.
Use its universal property to construct the canonical relative scheme and pullback square.
The smooth-universal family is the base change to M_{g,n}; the universal total stack can be smooth over Z even though its projection is nodal.
acceptance: The universal projection is not a smooth morphism at a node.

uses.how: For a stable genus-g family C/S, g≥2, the fibre product S×_{M̄_g} U_g is the PGL(5g−5)-torsor of projective frames of P(f_*ω³); it is representable smooth and surjective over S.

Given a stable ordered n-pointed family and an arbitrary section Δ, form K=coker(O_C→J_Δ∨⊕O_C(Σsᵢ)), with diagonal inclusion, and C^s=Proj_C Sym K. The two quotient maps at each old section and at Δ define the lifted ordered n+1 sections. This construction commutes with base change and is functorial under pointed isomorphisms. At a smooth new point it changes nothing, at a collision it inserts a marked rational tail, and at a node it inserts a marked rational bridge.

For the universal stable pointed curve f:C→M̄_{g,n}, define Lᵢ=sᵢ*ω_{C/M̄}. Each is an invertible sheaf because the marking is in the relative smooth locus; it identifies with sᵢ*Ω¹_{C/M̄}. Base change and relabelling preserve this line. The class ψᵢ=c₁(Lᵢ) is an exported input to the consumer’s tautological Chow-ring construction, not a new Chow theory here.

For g≥2 choose a representable finite surjective morphism V→M̄_g with V a normal integral scheme projective over Z. Pull back the universal stable curve to V. This is a chosen cover with a stable family, not a new fine moduli interpretation of V.

For the universal stable pointed family f:C→M̄_{g,n}, define E_{g,n}=f_*ω_{C/M̄}. It is locally free of rank g, including rank zero for g=0, and formation commutes with arbitrary base change with its canonical cocycle. The relative dualizing sheaf is untwisted by the markings.

nodes.title: Tricanonical Hilbert polynomial and frame rank
nodes.statement: Apply the parent’s pluricanonical vanishing, very-ampleness and cohomology/base-change API to a stable genus-g curve, g≥2. Its tricanonical direct image has rank 5g−5, the embedding is into P^{5g−6}, its degree is 6g−6 and its Hilbert polynomial is (6t−1)(g−1). These are the numerical inputs to the Hilbert moduli construction, not a second development of the parent’s curve cohomology.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Import the parent’s m≥2 vanishing and m≥3 very-ampleness with arbitrary-base-change locally free direct images.
Compute the degree of ω³ from deg ω=2g−2 and its Hilbert polynomial and rank by the parent’s Riemann–Roch.
acceptance: For m=3 the rank is 5g−5 and the projective dimension is 5g−6.

nodes.title: The tricanonical Hilbert locus
nodes.statement: For g≥2 let U_g be the locally closed locus in Hilb(P^{5g−6}_Z) with Hilbert polynomial (6t−1)(g−1) whose universal fibres are stable connected genus-g curves and whose hyperplane sheaf is ω³ with the complete basis of global sections. Its universal family and projective-frame interpretation identify U_g with tricanonically framed stable families. The canonical-line condition is included, not merely the Hilbert polynomial.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Use the universal flat Hilbert family with the stated polynomial.
Cut out the stable open locus and the canonical-polarization/frame condition using relative line-bundle comparison and base change.
The representing functor includes projective frames, hence a PGL(5g−5)-action.
acceptance: A curve with the same Hilbert polynomial but the wrong polarization is excluded.

nodes.statement: For a commutative ring A and γ,δ∈A define q_{γ,δ}(x,y)=x²+γxy+δy². Its nondegeneracy condition is that γ²−4δ is a unit. Over a field this describes a possibly nonsplit ordinary double point, including characteristic two. The definition is the polynomial form; the discriminant condition is an explicit hypothesis, not an arbitrary predicate field.

uses.how: Let A be a commutative ring, ε²=0, and d=γ²−4δ a unit. Every zero-constant-term series f=d(xu+yv) admits μ=−2δu+γv and ν=γu−2v such that q(x+εμ,y+εν)=q(x,y)+εf. The identity works also in characteristic two.

Let Λ be complete noetherian local with residue field k and let q over k have unit discriminant. hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including the zero ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. No noetherianity, regularity of A or unit discriminant is assumed for this polynomial-model statement.
proofSteps: For each actual j∈J choose a witness z of dz=bj, supplied by the native divisibility lemma.
Regularity of d makes that witness unique; apply cancellation to prove additivity and R-linearity.
The canonical map satisfies its denominator-free formula. The coordinate relation proves both generator values and regularity proves uniqueness.
acceptance: The notation b/d is explanatory only; no inverse or localization surrogate is used.

nodes.title: Residue of the section dual
nodes.statement: Set q=X²+γXY+δY², F=q(X,Y)−q(s,t), R=A[Y][X]/(F), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R). Construct the A-linear residue ρ:D→A as the second normal coordinate. It is surjective, ρ(ε)=1, and ker ρ is exactly the image of injective multiplication R→D. Furthermore ρ(zh)=ev(z)ρ(h). Hence D/R≅A with the section action.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including the zero ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. No noetherianity, regularity of A or unit discriminant is assumed for this polynomial-model statement.
proofSteps: Compose the checked normal equivalence with the native A-linear second projection. The pairs (0,α) prove surjectivity and ε has pair (0,1).
The inverse formula identifies zero residue exactly with maps j↦rj. The separate actual multiplication construction is injective by regularity of d.
Apply the independently derived correction/scalar-action formula to identify ρ(zh)=ev(z)ρ(h).
For nonzero A, a purported R-linear splitting has dσ(1)=σ(ev(d))=σ(0)=0. Pointwise regularity forces σ(1)=0, contradicting its right inverse property.
acceptance: For nonzero A, there is no R-linear section of ρ: d kills A but acts injectively on D.

nodes.title: Scalar correction in dual coordinates
nodes.statement: Set q=X²+γXY+δY², F=q(X,Y)−q(s,t), R=A[Y][X]/(F), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R). There is a unique A-linear K:R→R satisfying d K(r)=b(r−ι(ev r)). It obeys K(rz)=rK(z)+ι(ev z)K(r), K(c)=−a, K(d)=b and K(ια)=0.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring, including the zero ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. No noetherianity, regularity of A or unit discriminant is assumed for this polynomial-model statement.
proofSteps: Define the named A-linear K as the existing R-linear ε restricted to A, composed with the actual A-linear ideal projection p.
Its denominator-free formula is the dual-generator formula evaluated at p(r).
Multiplicativity of ev and ι and cancellation of d prove K(rz)=rK(z)+ι(ev(z))K(r).
The projection fixes c,d and kills coefficients, giving K(c)=−a, K(d)=b and K(ι(α))=0. Cancellation also proves uniqueness among all A-linear maps with the characterization.
acceptance: The product law uses ev(z) multiplying K(r); reversing that convention without changing the first term is incorrect.

uses.how: Both clutching morphisms are representable finite and unramified. For a fixed target stable curve their geometric fibres are finite choices of a node and, when relevant, an ordering or genus/marking assignment to its branches. These choices can be more than one even for a fixed separating genus and marking partition.

A pointed boundary type is a stable connected genus-g graph with n labelled legs and exactly one edge, up to label-preserving graph isomorphism, using the parent’s weighted dual graphs. Its normalization parameter stack is the product of the vertex moduli stacks modulo the finite automorphism group of this graph. For n=0,g≥2 the types are Δ₀ and Δᵢ for1≤i≤⌊g/2⌋, where Δ₀ is the closure of the nonseparating one-node locus, not merely the locus of irreducible nodal curves.
Under separating clutching, ξ*E_g≅pr₁*E_{g₁}⊕pr₂*E_{g₂}, hence ξ*λ_g≅pr₁*λ_{g₁}⊗pr₂*λ_{g₂}. The isomorphism is equivariant for permitted graph exchanges using the determinant convention.

The genus increases by one and both glued labels disappear. Exchanging these two sections gives the same glued target and is part of the graph automorphism quotient, including characteristic two.

proofSteps: Apply the parent’s self-clutching pushout with its base-change isomorphisms.
Use the parent graph-genus formula to obtain genus g.
acceptance: An unlabelled nonseparating node does not order its branches.

uses.how: Both clutching morphisms are representable finite and unramified. For a fixed target stable curve their geometric fibres are finite choices of a node and, when relevant, an ordering or genus/marking assignment to its branches. These choices can be more than one even for a fixed separating genus and marking partition.

A pointed boundary type is a stable connected genus-g graph with n labelled legs and exactly one edge, up to label-preserving graph isomorphism, using the parent’s weighted dual graphs. Its normalization parameter stack is the product of the vertex moduli stacks modulo the finite automorphism group of this graph. For n=0,g≥2 the types are Δ₀ and Δᵢ for1≤i≤⌊g/2⌋, where Δ₀ is the closure of the nonseparating one-node locus, not merely the locus of irreducible nodal curves.

For ξ_irr there is an exact sequence0→E_{g−1,n+2}→ξ_irr*E_{g,n}→O→0 with the last map the residue at an ordered branch. It gives ξ_irr*λ_g≅λ_{g−1,n+2}. Exchanging the two branches negates the residue; the induced equivariant determinant data must retain this sign when descending to the unlabelled graph quotient.

uses.how: The normalization of the reduced total boundary of M̄_{g,n} is the disjoint union, over stable one-edge types, of the corresponding vertex-product quotient stacks. Its finite map to the boundary records a distinguished node; it separates branches at curves with several nodes of the same type.

For π:M̄_{g,n+1}→M̄_{g,n} and retained i, let D_{i,n+1} be the divisor of a rational tail carrying exactly marks i,n+1 and its attachment. Then Lᵢ on the source is π*Lᵢ⊗O(D_{i,n+1}); equivalently π*Lᵢ=Lᵢ⊗O(−D_{i,n+1}).

For g≥2 let Δ be the effective Cartier divisor M̄_g minus M_g, with coefficient1 on each reduced local node branch. Its global decomposition is Δ=Σ_{i=0}^{⌊g/2⌋}Δᵢ according to the one-edge unpointed types. For a generically smooth stable family over an integral noetherian S, its pullback is an effective Cartier divisor Δ_S; arbitrary families mapping entirely into Δ do not have this effective-Cartier pullback.

Over the generic one-node locus the quotient gives a unique unlabelled node; finite birational normality identifies each normalization component.

nodes.statement: For the universal stable pointed curve f:C→M̄_{g,n}, define Lᵢ=sᵢ*ω_{C/M̄}. The class ψᵢ=c₁(Lᵢ) is an exported input to the consumer’s tautological Chow-ring construction, not a new Chow theory here.

nodes.title: Coarse spaces of pointed curve stacks
nodes.statement: For each stable pair construct the coarse algebraic spaces q:M̄_{g,n}→M̄^{coarse}_{g,n} and q°:M_{g,n}→M^{coarse}_{g,n}. They are initial for maps to algebraic spaces and induce bijections between geometric points and isomorphism classes. Stable coarse spaces are proper over Z. Existence alone gives neither smoothness of the coarse space nor a universal family on it; base change is used only with the hypotheses of the imported coarse-space theorem.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: The finite diagonal gives finite inertia; apply the generic coarse-space existence theorem with its noetherian finite-type hypotheses.
Use the proper coarse-space comparison to deduce properness.
Restrict the stable coarse space to the saturated smooth open; geometric curve smoothness is invariant under isomorphism.
acceptance: Smooth stacks can have singular coarse spaces.

uses.how: Let S be a proper finite-type algebraic space over an algebraically closed field and f:X→S a stable genus-g family g≥2 whose coarse moduli map has finite geometric fibres. For all sufficiently large d, det f_*ω^{3d} is ample on S.
For g≥2 M̄^{coarse}_g is a projective scheme over Z. There is a positive power of a sufficiently high pluricanonical determinant which descends to an ample line on the coarse algebraic space.

The fixed symplectic component M_g[N] over Z[1/N,ζ_N] is a smooth quasi-projective scheme of relative dimension3g−3, carrying a smooth projective universal curve of genus g. Forgetting level to M_g is representable finite étale. It is regular; geometric irreducibility is the separate connectedness theorem.

For an integral finite-type base S over a field and a smooth genus-g family, g≥2, maximal variation means that the coarse classifying map S→M_g^{coarse} is generically quasi-finite onto its image. The definition uses geometric curve isomorphism classes, not choices of frames or markings.

Over an algebraically closed field k, the coarse stable curve moduli admits a morphism t̄:M̄_g^{coarse}→A_g^{min} extending smooth Torelli. On a stable curve it uses the abelian part of the generalized Jacobian and maps to the corresponding minimal-compactification stratum. The descended rational Hodge line satisfies λ_coarse=t̄*ω_min, with ω_min ample.

nodes.title: Nef pluricanonical direct images
nodes.statement: For a family f:X→B of stable genus-g curves g≥2 over a smooth projective curve B over an algebraically closed field, f_*ω^m is nef for m≥2, in every characteristic. Nefness means nonnegative degree for line quotients after finite maps from smooth projective curves.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: If the generic fibre is smooth apply the smooth-generic direct-image theorem.
Otherwise split persistent nodes after a finite cover of B and use the normalization residue sequence.

Its kernel is the direct sum of component bundles twisted by (m−1)D^ν, nef by the pointed theorem, and its quotient is a direct sum of O_B. Apply preservation of nefness under extensions from the positivity supplier.
Descend nefness along the finite cover.
acceptance: Characteristic two is included; the exceptional bound≤1 still contradicts H¹≥2.

Use finite generation of the relative ideal and a sufficiently large degree to recover the saturated ideal; record this generic projective-algebra input as a supplier request.

nodes.statement: Let S be a proper finite-type algebraic space over an algebraically closed field and f:X→S a stable genus-g family g≥2 whose coarse moduli map has finite geometric fibres. For all sufficiently large d, det f_*ω^{3d} is ample on S.

Its projective-frame classifying map to the Grassmannian quotient has finite fibres because its kernel determines the embedded curve up to projectivity.

Use the precise ampleness lemma: for a nef vector bundle E on a proper algebraic space and a locally free quotient SymᵈE→Q with finite-fibre classifying map, det Q is ample. This generic positivity theorem is not silently attributed to SF.5; it is recorded as an unassigned extension gap.

nodes.title: Full symplectic level on smooth curves
nodes.statement: Fix g≥2 and N≥3 invertible on the base. A full Jacobi level structure on a smooth genus-g curve is an isomorphism α:(Z/N)^{2g}→J(C)[N] carrying the standard alternating form to the Weil pairing through a chosen trivialization of μ_N, or equivalently a homogeneous symplectic-similitude identification without choosing that trivialization. Use the fixed symplectic flavour over Z[1/N,ζ_N], and the similitude flavour over Z[1/N]. Their components and universal families are not identified without this choice.
hypotheses: The full range, base and auxiliary data are specified in the statement; none are suppressed by a global stable-pair convention.
proofSteps: Use the relative Jacobian of the smooth curve family, its principal polarization and prime-to-characteristic torsion pairing; the curve-relative representability input is a recorded extension gap.
Define the isomorphism functor with its exact pairing condition and marking-preserving curve isomorphisms.
acceptance: N is invertible; level at the characteristic is a different problem.

nodes.title: Torsion freeness of the stable-stack Picard group
nodes.statement: For g≥2 Pic(M̄_{g,C}) is torsion free. A torsion line gives a finite cyclic cover of the stack. Over Teichmüller space this cover splits; its character factors through the mapping-class group, and extending over every boundary kills each Dehn-twist generator, so the cover and line are trivial.

Use the one-node smoothing monodromy to identify the boundary loop with the corresponding Dehn twist.
Since the cover extends over that divisor, its cyclic monodromy on the loop vanishes; all generators vanish.
acceptance: Retain stack stabilizers; passing first to the coarse space is not this proof.

nodes.title: The degree-d level Picard parameter functor
nodes.statement: For g≥2, N≥3 invertible with a fixed pairing component, and d∈Z, define the parameter sheaf P_g,N^d=Pic^d_{C_g/M_g[N]} on the fppf site. It parametrizes sheafified relative degree-d line classes on the universal smooth curve. An algebraically closed field point corresponds to a triple (C,α,L) up to curve-level isomorphism and line-bundle isomorphism. Over a general base T the sheaf class can have a Brauer obstruction to a globally existing line bundle; the triple groupoid and this sheaf are distinct.

proofSteps: Pull back the relative Picard sheaf of the universal curve, including the degree decomposition and arbitrary-base-change comparison.
The Jacobian extension must supply representability of Picᵈ as a torsor under Pic⁰; it does not assert a universal line without rigidification.
Over an algebraically closed field the Brauer obstruction vanishes, giving the stated triples.
acceptance: The Picard parameter is a sheaf of classes, not the automorphism groupoid of line bundles.

nodes.title: Coefficient base change of the actual dual quotient
nodes.statement: Let A be any commutative ring, γ,δ,s,t∈A, q=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), u=[X], v=[Y], ι:A→R, c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδv+ιδ·ιt+ιγu, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m(r)(j)=rj, ev:R→A the section evaluation and ε the unique dual generator dε(j)=bj. Construct the canonical A′-linear equivalence E_{Q,f}:A′⊗_A Q≃Q′ satisfying E_{Q,f}(a′⊗[h])=[E_D(a′⊗h)] and E_Q′(E_{Q,f}(a′⊗z))=a′f(E_Q(z)). hypotheses: All coefficient rings are commutative and may have zero divisors or be the zero ring. No noetherianity, unit discriminant, injectivity or flatness of f is required. Statements concern the explicit polynomial model, not arbitrary nodal families.

Evaluate E_D in normal coordinates: it takes r incl+ιαε to the corresponding primed expression, sends ε to ε′, and its residue is a′f(ρh). This proves the quotient-representative formula agrees with the constructed equivalence.
Identity and composition follow from the residue formula and injectivity of E_Q′; no tensor left-exactness or flatness of f is assumed.
acceptance: Nonflat specialization ℤ→F₂ with γ=1,δ=s=t=0 preserves the actual quotient and sends its residue generator to residue 1.

nodes.statement: A is any commutative ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. R=A[Y][X]/(X²+γYX+δY²−q(s,t)), c=u−s,d=v−t, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m:R→D, m(r)(j)=rj, Q=D/im(m). nodes.title: Faithful detection for the residue quotient
nodes.statement: A is any commutative ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. R=A[Y][X]/(X²+γYX+δY²−q(s,t)), c=u−s,d=v−t, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m:R→D, m(r)(j)=rj, Q=D/im(m). If B is a faithfully flat R-algebra and f:Q→_R Q, then 1_B⊗f is bijective if and only if f is bijective.
hypotheses: A is any commutative ring; γ,δ,s,t∈A. R=A[Y][X]/(X²+γYX+δY²−q(s,t)), c=u−s,d=v−t, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), m:R→D, m(r)(j)=rj, Q=D/im(m).

proofSteps: Apply the pinned faithful-flat bijectivity theorem to the actual R-module Q.
Transport along E_Q when working with Q_B. Faithfulness is separately required; a flat localization away from the section kills Q.

nodes.title: The actual dual coefficient-Hom map
nodes.statement: For any commutative ring A and γ,δ,s,t∈A, let q(X,Y)=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), ι:A→R the actual coefficient algebra map, u=[X], v=[Y], c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδv+ιδ·ιt+ιγu, J=(c,d), D=Hom_R(J,R), incl:J→R and ε∈D with dε(j)=bj. Put Φ=((a,b),(−c,d)), Ψ=((d,−b),(c,a)), P_J(z)=cz₀−dz₁, P_D(z)=z₀incl−z₁ε and p(z)=(-z₁,z₀). For any A-module M, set N_M=R⊗_A M with the inherited left R-action, and U_M(f)=f⊗_A id_M on the actual native tensors. Use the already-built finite-product tensor and finite-free Hom coordinates E_M:R²⊗_A M≃ₗ[A]Hom_R(R²,N_M), E_M(z⊗m)(w)=(w₀z₀+w₁z₁)⊗m. Construct the R-linear map θ_D,M:D⊗_A M→Hom_R(J,N_M), characterized on pure tensors by θ_D,M(h⊗m)(j)=h(j)⊗m.
hypotheses: A is an arbitrary commutative ring; M is an arbitrary A-module, with no flatness hypothesis.
All tensor actions and Hom spaces are the actual native inherited ones; no noetherianity, nontriviality or unit-discriminant assumption is imposed for this polynomial calculation.
proofSteps: Apply the pinned heterobasic tensor lift to (h,m)↦(j↦h(j)⊗m). Verify R-linearity in h and j and A-balancing in m using the inherited scalar tower.
The source is the actual R-linear dual D; the target has the inherited left R-action on R⊗_A M.
acceptance: The statement uses the actual section ideal and actual R-linear dual in the untruncated polynomial ring.
Keep this algebra calculation separate from higher Ext, relative stable-reflexivity, completed-local and family/sheaf descent.

nodes.statement: For every commutative ring A and γ,δ,s,t∈A, use the actual R=A[Y][X]/(X²+γXY+δY²−(s²+γst+δt²)), u=[X], v=[Y], coefficient map ι, J=(u−ιs,v−ιt), D=Hom_R(J,R) and N=R⊗_A M for an arbitrary A-module M. Write c=u−ιs, d=v−ιt, b=u+ιs+ιγ·ιt, a=ιδ·v+ιδ·ιt+ιγ·u; Φ=((a,b),(−c,d)), Ψ=((d,−b),(c,a)). The actual finite-free resolutions C(false), C(true) have R² in every degree and differential B(e,n)=Φ if (n mod2=0)⇔e=true, otherwise Ψ, with signed augmentations P_J(z)=cz₀−dz₁ and P_D(z)=z₀incl−z₁ε. H(e,M) denotes the inherited actual R-linear Hom cochain with differential h↦h∘B(e,n). The forward native R-linear map of sectionDualDerivedExtIso sends zero to zero in every degree.

nodes.title: Canonical coefficient exchange for the section dual
nodes.statement: Let A be any commutative ring, γ,δ,s,t∈A, q(X,Y)=X²+γXY+δY², R=A[Y][X]/(q(X,Y)−q(s,t)), ι:A→R the coefficient algebra map, u=[X], v=[Y], J=(u−ιs,v−ιt) and D=Hom_R(J,R). All duals are R-linear and use native Module.Dual. For any A-module M put N_M=R⊗_A M with its inherited left R-action and η=Module.Dual.eval R J. The canonical exchange Φ_D,M:D∨⊗_A M≃ₗ[R]Hom_R(D,N_M) is an equivalence with Φ_D,M(F⊗m)(h)=F(h)⊗m. Construct it as (η⁻¹⊗id_M) followed by the existing Θ_J,M.
hypotheses: No noetherianity, reducedness, nonzero coefficient ring, unit discriminant or flatness of M is assumed. Ext vanishing is only in positive degrees.
proofSteps: Tensor the explicit native bidual equivalence with id_M using the heterobasic R-linear tensor equivalence.
Compose its inverse direction with Θ_J,M. On pure tensors, η(η⁻¹F)(h)=F(h) proves that the result is the actual canonical exchange map.
Tensor induction gives uniqueness and naturality for every A-linear map M→M′.
acceptance: Use the actual ideal subtype, native R-duals and R-module tensor action. No private stable-reflexivity predicate or replacement Ext carrier is introduced.
This polynomial calculation does not supply the two-base completion comparison, pointed formal hull or family/sheaf descent.
